thread:
maria (eng-runtime): Heads-up — the Dedicated rollout to eu-west-1 is blocked. We're seeing a ~2.3x p95 token-latency regression after the merge of PR #3456 (kernel-selector rewrite). Can we triage? :exclamation:

sasha (eng-infra): Noted. CI perf job flagged it on the nightly performance suite, but the canary in prod also shows the same for customer pool `dedicated-eu-42`.

li (eng-ml): Quick snapshot from the profiler on a single request (seq_len 512):
```
Stage: attention
old-kernel: 28.7ms
new-kernel: 64.1ms
KV cache hit path: new-kernel falls back to slow path
batching: per-batch token throughput decreased
```
This smells like the kernel selection heuristics choose a suboptimal kernel for shorter kv-cache warm paths.

josh (eng-sre): Deploy-bot reported throttles increasing and SLA p99 crossing 500ms -> currently SLA target is 250ms for this pool. Customer impact: two customers reported higher latencies in support channel.

samir (eng-platform): Which commit introduced it? Can we bisect? I can run a binary-level comparison across the last 7 merges.

maria (eng-runtime): Start with PR #3456 -> PR #3472 (batching heuristics tweak) -> #3490 (quant path polishing). My suspicion: the kernel-selector rewrite in #3456 changed fallback ordering so certain attention shapes pick a generic kernel that is slower on our Ampere instances.

sasha (eng-infra): I kicked off a git bisect on the release branch: `git bisect start 1768000...1769123` then tested with the perf harness. Early result: bad commit 9f2a8b3 (PR #3456) -> good commit 1ab3c44.

maria (eng-runtime): Thanks. Can you paste the micro-bench numbers?

sasha (eng-infra): Micro-bench (attention-only, 512x512 tokens, fp16, 1 GPU):
```
commit 1ab3c44: 24.9ms
commit 9f2a8b3: 60.3ms
```
Also reproduced on dedicated staging pool.

li (eng-ml): Kernel chooser is now using `flops_estimate * memory_penalty` heuristic. For these shapes the memory_penalty overweights the fused-gemm path and chooses the generic kernel. We used to bias toward fused kernels for small sequence lengths.

maria (eng-runtime): So fix options: revert the selector logic in #3456, add a targeted guard that forces fused kernel for attention shapes < 1024, or ship a canary rollback for the dedicated pools. Which is lowest-risk?

samir (eng-platform): Canary rollback buys us breathing room while we prepare a proper patch. But note: rollback must not touch quantization changes from #3490 which are safe.

josh (eng-sre): Ops: marking rollout blocked, notifying CS + customers. If we don't mitigate within 2 hours, we'll need to roll back to previous stable image for all dedicated pools to meet SLA.

maria (eng-runtime): I'm going to prepare a minimal revert PR that only changes kernel selection ordering back to the previous weights. Will keep batching heuristics from other PRs. PR draft: #3512.

sasha (eng-infra): Deploy-bot: can we schedule a canary deploy of the revert to `dedicated-eu-42` now? If it recovers p95 to baseline, we rollout.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy queued: image rwd/inference:release-1768900-revert-3512 -> pool `dedicated-eu-42` (10% traffic). Health checks: latency, rejects, error-rate.

li (eng-ml): Observed behavior to watch after revert: KV cache hit-path (should return to previous fast fused kernel), batch-formation latency (ensure no regression in batching overhead). If canary looks good, we still want a follow-up to add a regression test in CI that covers the attention shapes that regressed.

maria (eng-runtime): +1 on CI regression. I'll add a perf-test case that runs attention microbench for seq=256,512,1024 and fails if p95 exceeds baseline+20%. PR coming after revert.

sasha (eng-infra): Canary metrics after 3 minutes: p95 token latency dropped from 820ms -> 340ms on the canary nodes. Error rates stable. Looks promising.

josh (eng-sre): Can you confirm customer queues are returning to normal? CS says one impacted customer reported >2x latency earlier — they should see improvements if this holds.

maria (eng-runtime): I'm merging the minimal revert and requesting a full rollback if the canary fails in the next 10 minutes. Also filing a postmortem stub: link to doc (internal) and tagging owners for follow-through: kernel selector unit tests + CI perf coverage.

samir (eng-platform): After revert, let's schedule a short load test on Dedicated staging to validate HVG/low-latency tail under multi-tenant burst. Also add an alert on kernel-selector fallback rate so we catch this earlier.

li (eng-ml): I'll add an instrumentation event when the chooser prefers non-fused kernels for shapes < 1024 so we can trigger alerts.

maria (eng-runtime): Thanks all. Great cross-team response. Leaving the thread open for postmortem notes. :white_check_mark:
